finding: Acceptance verified at source 9 August 2026 — with a dating caveat this Index is recording against itself. Sotheby's own bidder guidance was read in full this session, having previously been cited rather than opened. Where a lot is designated “Cryptocurrency Payments,” Sotheby's accepts BTC, ETH and USDC, and states in its own words that “payments from self-hosted wallets will not be accepted”, listing five permitted custodians: Coinbase Custody Trust; Coinbase, Inc.; Fidelity Digital Assets Services; Gemini Trust Company; and Paxos Trust Company. A hardware wallet therefore cannot pay Sotheby's directly. ⚠️ The caveat: both pages carrying that rule are dated 2021 — the bidder's guide is stamped 10 June 2021 and says the restriction applies “for this auction”, and the payment-information article is stamped 12 May 2021 and is scoped to a single lot. So the honest reading is that when Sotheby's has taken cryptocurrency it has required a named custodial wallet and refused self-custody — published per sale, five years ago — rather than that this is standing policy today. Confirm the terms for the specific lot before bidding. Coin badges are held: Sotheby's names its accepted currencies explicitly, so the issue is the age and scope of the evidence, not its specificity. Source: sothebys.com/en/buy-sell/cryptocurrency-faq
